admission.justification: A held `j` can outrun the answer that brings the next family. "No later change in this tree" then stands beside a later change and tells the reader the walk is over when it is not. A status cleared by an update made while rendering comes back, because React can apply a queued status after that render. The rule is realized in the traversal hook and in the tree component, and a case on the hook alone and mounted cases guard it.

applicability: The polite status of `j`/`k` and of the visible previous-change and next-change controls in the reviewer's family tree: the end messages and the message of the stop at a continuation control.
conditions: What the tree shows is named by the order it lists in and, for each family shown under the filter, the family and the number of its member rows returned. A filter, the order control, a roster continuation and a selection's answer that brings or drops a family each change it.
No render shows the message beside other rows, the first such render included, and no state is updated while rendering.
Saying the same message again for the same rows changes no state, so a key held at an end renders nothing.
A new move gets its own message.
exclusions: The wording of the messages and which rows are stops.
statement: The message of the last traversal move is shown only beside the rows the tree showed when it was said: once the tree has shown other rows the message is dropped and does not return when the tree shows the same rows again.
